# Adaptate

> One schema. Each part of the app checks only the fields it uses. A screen, a form, an API client, or a stream.

# Docs

Source: docs/index.md

---
title: "Docs"
description: "Where to read about views, streaming, OpenAPI, types, and the generated API."
---

# Docs

One schema. Each part of the app checks only the fields it uses. A screen, a form, an API client, or a stream.

A React component that checks its own view is [examples/react-view](../examples/react-view). Vue, Svelte, and Solid can call `transformSchema` the same way. This repository includes the React example.

The pages below stay in this folder so a later docs site can pick them up. Each page has a `title` and a `description`. [llms.txt](../llms.txt) lists them for agents. [llms-full.txt](../llms-full.txt) contains the page text.

## Guides

- [Transform](transform.md): one Zod schema, and a config that marks which fields each screen requires.
- [Streaming](streaming.md): check a tool call while the JSON is still arriving.
- [Incremental partial JSON](incremental-parser.md): scan each new character of a JSON stream once.
- [OpenAPI](openapi.md): turn an OpenAPI schema into Zod, and write a Zod schema back out.
- [Effect](effect.md): run the same checks in an Effect pipeline.
- [TypeScript](typescript.md): types ship in the package and are checked on TypeScript 7 and 6.
- [Subpaths](subpaths.md): the published entry points, and which peers each one loads.
- [Optional peers](optional-peers.md): effect, js-yaml, and the ref parser load only when that code is imported.
- [Performance](performance.md): measured cost of import, a full document, four component views, a streaming check, and bundle size.
- [Proof](proof.md): each front-page sentence mapped to a test, a script, or a CI job.
- [Migration 2.4](migration-2.4.md): YAML and the ref parser became optional peers.
- [Development](development.md): install, test, and build this repository.

## API

- [API reference](api/index.md): generated from the `.d.ts` files that ship in the packages.


# Transform

Source: docs/transform.md

---
title: "Transform"
description: "One Zod schema, and a config that marks which fields each screen requires."
---

# Transform

`transformSchema(schema, config)` returns a Zod schema with the configured fields required. Unmentioned fields stay as they were.

Config values:

- `true` — strip optionality
- `false` — keep the field optional
- nested object — recurse
- `{ '*': config }` — apply `config` to each array element
- `(data) => boolean` or `{ requiredIf: (data) => boolean }` — with `makeConditionalSchemaTransformer` only

```ts
import { z } from "zod";
import { transformSchema, type Config } from "@adaptate/core";

const schema = z.deepPartial(
  z.object({
    name: z.string(),
    age: z.number(),
    address: z.object({
      street: z.string(),
      city: z.string(),
    }),
  }),
);

const config = {
  name: true,
  age: true,
  address: { city: true },
} satisfies Config<z.infer<typeof schema>>;

const updatedSchema = transformSchema(schema, config);
updatedSchema.parse({ name: "Davin", age: 30, address: { city: "Pettit" } });
const streetOnly = updatedSchema.safeParse({
  name: "Davin",
  age: 30,
  address: { street: "Main St" },
});
```

`streetOnly.success` is false: `city` is required.

Zod 4 exports `z.deepPartial`. The object method `.deepPartial()` is the Zod 3 method. The same config works when each field is written with `.optional()` instead of `z.deepPartial`.

`Config<T>` checks field paths at compile time, including `'*'` on arrays:

```ts
import { z } from "zod";
import { type Config } from "@adaptate/core";

const userSchema = z.object({
  name: z.string(),
  address: z.object({ street: z.string(), city: z.string() }),
  tags: z.array(z.string()),
});

const config = {
  name: true,
  address: { city: true },
  tags: { "*": true },
} satisfies Config<z.infer<typeof userSchema>>;
```

`makeConditionalSchemaTransformer(data)(schema, config)` applies `requiredIf` against that `data`.

```ts
import { z } from "zod";
import { makeConditionalSchemaTransformer } from "@adaptate/core";

const schema = z.object({
  parentContactNumber: z.number().optional(),
  age: z.number().optional(),
});
const config = {
  parentContactNumber: { requiredIf: (data: { age?: number }) => (data.age ?? 0) < 18 },
  age: true,
};
const transformer = makeConditionalSchemaTransformer({ age: 17 })(schema, config);
transformer.run(); // throws: parentContactNumber is required
```

- `transformer.schema` — the transformed Zod schema
- `transformer.run()` — `transformer.schema.parse(data)`
- `transformer.staticConfig` — the config with conditionals removed, for `transformSchema`

Traversal, from `packages/core/src/index.ts`:

1. An optional field is unwrapped with `.unwrap()`.
2. Nested objects recurse with the nested config.
3. An array `'*'` config is applied to the element schema.
4. The new shape is copied back with object spread into `z.object`.

Fields absent from the config are kept. [DESIGN.md](../DESIGN.md) walks through the recursion and states O(N) time and O(D) space.


# Streaming

Source: docs/streaming.md

---
title: "Streaming"
description: "Check a tool call while the JSON is still arriving."
---

# Streaming

`@adaptate/core/stream` checks a partial document against each named config while text is still arriving. `zod` is the only peer.

`parsePartialJson(text)` closes open strings, objects, and arrays, then `JSON.parse`s the longest prefix that parses. It returns `undefined` when nothing parses.

`createStreamValidator(schema, configs)` builds the schemas it can at creation:

- `partial(value)` checks the value with one lenient schema cached on the base schema object (`WeakMap`). The cache is filled on the first partial check, not when the validator is constructed, so a strict schema built from the same fields is left alone. Building that lenient schema does not parse the source object or array. Absent fields stay optional. Present fields are still type-checked. Every named config receives that same check. Editing a config does not change `partial`, because a missing field stays optional for every config.
- `final(value)` runs `transformSchema(schema, config).safeParse(value)` for every named config and returns `{ valid, errors }` per name. This `final` takes a value, not text. Those transformed schemas are built when the validator is created and then reused. The lenient partial schema is cached on the base schema object with a `WeakMap`, so it is collected with that schema. Config objects are read at creation: editing one afterward leaves the schema that was already built. A config that cannot be transformed fails inside `final`, not while the validator is constructed. `transformSchema` itself still builds a schema on every direct call.

`validateStructuredOutput({ partial, final }, schema, configs)` runs those two methods when the corresponding field is not `null`.

`createAgUiPartialValidator(schema, configs)` returns a push function. It appends `delta` to a buffer keyed by `toolCallId` for `TOOL_CALL_ARGS` and by `messageId` for `TEXT_MESSAGE_CONTENT`, then calls `parsePartialJson` on that buffer. A parsed value is checked with `partial`. A chunk that does not parse returns `undefined`. `TOOL_CALL_END` and `TEXT_MESSAGE_END` drop that id. `push.close(id)` drops it too. The same name on `@adaptate/core/stream-incremental` tokenizes each chunk once through `createPartialJsonFeed`. See [Incremental partial JSON](incremental-parser.md).

```ts
import { z } from "zod";
import { createAgUiPartialValidator } from "@adaptate/core/stream";

const recipe = z.object({
  title: z.string().optional(),
  servings: z.number().optional(),
});
const push = createAgUiPartialValidator(recipe, {
  card: { title: true },
});
push({
  type: "TOOL_CALL_ARGS",
  toolCallId: "call-1",
  delta: '{"title":"Pas',
});
```

Streams partial JSON without re-reading what it already saw. The run metadata and the per-chunk numbers are in [Performance](performance.md#measured).


# Incremental partial JSON

Source: docs/incremental-parser.md

---
title: "Incremental partial JSON"
description: "Tokenize a JSON stream once and reuse closed values."
---

# Incremental partial JSON

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  chunk["New chunk"] --> read["Read each new character once"]
  read --> token["Finish a string, number, literal, or bracket"]
  token --> stack["Append it to the open container"]
  stack --> copy["Copy only the containers still open"]
  copy --> check["Check that value"]
```

`fromAsyncIterable` reads an async sequence of strings or UTF-8 bytes. Byte chunks go through `TextDecoder` with `stream: true`, and the decoder flushes after the source ends. `push` still receives a string.

```ts
import { Readable } from "node:stream";
import { fromAsyncIterable } from "@adaptate/core/stream-incremental";

const partials: unknown[] = [];
const readable = Readable.from([
  new TextEncoder().encode('{"title":"Pas'),
  new TextEncoder().encode('ta"}'),
]);

for await (const partialValue of fromAsyncIterable(readable)) {
  partials.push(partialValue);
}

type OpenAiEvent = {
  choices?: Array<{
    delta?: {
      tool_calls?: Array<{ function?: { arguments?: string } }>;
    };
  }>;
};

async function* openAiArguments(events: Iterable<OpenAiEvent> | AsyncIterable<OpenAiEvent>) {
  for await (const event of events) {
    const delta = event.choices?.[0]?.delta?.tool_calls?.[0]?.function?.arguments;
    if (typeof delta === "string" && delta.length > 0) yield delta;
  }
}

type AnthropicEvent = {
  delta?: { type?: string; partial_json?: string };
};

async function* anthropicInputJson(
  events: Iterable<AnthropicEvent> | AsyncIterable<AnthropicEvent>,
) {
  for await (const event of events) {
    const delta = event.delta;
    if (delta?.type === "input_json_delta" && typeof delta.partial_json === "string") {
      yield delta.partial_json;
    }
  }
}

const openAiEvents: OpenAiEvent[] = [
  {
    choices: [{ delta: { tool_calls: [{ function: { arguments: '{"title":"Pas' } }] } }],
  },
];
const anthropicEvents: AnthropicEvent[] = [
  { delta: { type: "input_json_delta", partial_json: '{"title":"Pas' } },
];

for await (const partialValue of fromAsyncIterable(openAiArguments(openAiEvents))) {
  partials.push(partialValue);
}
for await (const partialValue of fromAsyncIterable(anthropicInputJson(anthropicEvents))) {
  partials.push(partialValue);
}
```

`Readable` from Node, a Web `ReadableStream`, and either delta mapping are the same input: strings or bytes. No SDK is required.

Each chunk is tokenized once. A finished string, number, literal, or member is appended to the open container. An open string keeps the decoded prefix and any pending escape, so a push reads only the new characters. `push` copies the deepest open container and reuses the cached copies along the spine. Closed values stay the same object. On the grocery order in `bench/ab/order.js`, the incremental feed reads each character once. Partial JSON tests assert `visits` equals the text length. `parsePartialJson` still walks a whole prefix, and `@adaptate/core/stream` keeps that path. `createPartialJsonFeed` and `createAgUiPartialValidator` on `@adaptate/core/stream-incremental` use the tokenizer. A value is checked with the lenient partial. A whitespace chunk keeps the previous value and its check. `createFrameThrottle` stays on `@adaptate/core/stream`. It keeps the latest value and emits it on the next frame, or on `setTimeout(0)` when there is no `requestAnimationFrame`.


# OpenAPI

Source: docs/openapi.md

---
title: "OpenAPI"
description: "Turn an OpenAPI schema into Zod, and write a Zod schema back out."
---

# OpenAPI

`@adaptate/utils` converts OpenAPI schemas and Zod schemas, and loads a spec. Peer: `zod@^3.25.0 || ^4.0.0`. See [Optional peers](optional-peers.md) for YAML and remote `$ref`s.

```ts
import { getDereferencedOpenAPIDocument, openAPISchemaToZod, zodToOpenAPISchema } from "@adaptate/utils";
import { z } from "zod";

const doc = await getDereferencedOpenAPIDocument({
  location: "filesystem",
  callSiteURL: import.meta.url,
  relativePathToSpecFile: "./api-spec.yml",
});

const fromWeb = await getDereferencedOpenAPIDocument({
  location: "web",
  webURL: "https://api.apis.guru/v2/specs/googleapis.com/books/v1/openapi.yaml",
});

const zodSchema = openAPISchemaToZod({
  type: "object",
  required: ["age"],
  properties: {
    name: { type: "string", minLength: 2 },
    age: { type: "integer", minimum: 0 },
    email: { type: "string", format: "email" },
    tags: { type: "array", items: { type: "string" }, minItems: 1 },
  },
});
zodSchema.parse({ name: "Ada", age: 25, email: "ada@example.com", tags: ["dev"] });

const openAPISchema = zodToOpenAPISchema(
  z.object({
    name: z.string().min(2).describe("Full name"),
    age: z.number().int().min(0),
    email: z.email().optional(),
    tags: z.array(z.string()).min(1),
  }),
);
```

`openAPISchemaToZod` supports `string`, `number`, `integer`, `boolean`, `object`, `array`, `enum`, `minLength`, `maxLength`, `pattern`, string `format` (email, uuid, url, date-time, date), `minimum` / `maximum`, `exclusiveMinimum` / `exclusiveMaximum`, `multipleOf`, `minItems` / `maxItems`, `allOf` (`.and()`), `anyOf` / `oneOf` (`.union()`), `nullable`, object `required`, and a `$ref` that is already resolved.

`zodToOpenAPISchema` writes `required` without `.optional()` fields, `.nullable()`, string min/max/regex/formats, number min/max (inclusive and exclusive), `multipleOf`, integer, array `minItems` / `maxItems`, `z.enum` (string enums and numeric member tuples; Zod 4 folded `z.nativeEnum` into `z.enum`), `z.union` as `anyOf`, `.describe()`, `ZodDate`, and `ZodBigInt`.

`json-schema-to-zod` and `zod-to-json-schema` cover cases these two functions do not.


# Effect

Source: docs/effect.md

---
title: "Effect"
description: "Run the same checks in an Effect pipeline. Effect is an optional peer."
---

# Effect

`@adaptate/core/effect` needs the optional peer `effect@^4.0.0`. Importing `@adaptate/core` or `@adaptate/core/stream` does not load `effect`. Validation is not retried.

```ts
import { Effect } from "effect";
import { z } from "zod";
import { createEffectStreamValidator } from "@adaptate/core/effect";

const recipe = z.object({
  title: z.string().optional(),
  servings: z.number().optional(),
});
const validator = createEffectStreamValidator(recipe, {
  card: { title: true },
  kitchen: { servings: true },
});

const report = Effect.runSync(validator.final('{"title":"Pasta"}'));
// report.value is { title: "Pasta" }
// report.configs.card is { valid: true, issues: null }
// report.configs.kitchen.valid is false

const card = Effect.runSync(validator.final('{"title":"Pasta"}', "card"));
// { title: "Pasta" }
```

`createEffectStreamValidator` builds the per-config `transformSchema` results when the validator is created, and `final(text)` reuses them. The lenient partial schema is cached on the base schema at the first partial check. A schema that cannot be transformed, such as `z.string()`, still fails inside `final` with `configName: "schema"`. Config objects are read at creation. `final(text, configName)` calls `transformSchema` for that config.

`final(text)` parses with `JSON.parse`. Bad or truncated text fails with `AdaptateParseError`. The base schema is then parsed; that failure is `AdaptateValidationError` with `configName: "schema"`. On success the effect succeeds with `{ value, configs }`. Each named config is `{ valid, issues }`. An unmet config does not fail the effect. A mutated config is read by value on the next `final`.

`final(text, configName)` parses, then validates with `transformSchema(schema, configs[configName])`. Failure is `AdaptateValidationError` with that `configName`. Success is the parsed value. `configName` is typed as `keyof` the configs object. If the runtime name is not an own key of `configs`, the effect fails with `AdaptateValidationError` and one custom issue, `unknown config`, instead of validating the base schema. A mutated config is read on this path, because this path calls `transformSchema` again.

`validate(schema, config, value)` is `transformSchema(schema, config).parse`, failing as `AdaptateValidationError` with `configName: "config"`.

`validatePartial(schema, configs, partial)` fails on the first config that has errors, keeping that config's Zod issues. A thrown `ZodError` is kept as issues. Any other thrown cause becomes one custom issue with the error message.

`partial(value)` is the lenient stream report. `agUi(event)` and `agUiStream(events)` wrap `createAgUiPartialValidator` from `@adaptate/core/stream`. That path appends to a buffer and calls `parsePartialJson`. It does not load `@adaptate/core/stream-incremental`. Pass a third argument, `makeFeed`, and those two methods call that feed instead. Omit it and they keep the re-parse feed.


# TypeScript

Source: docs/typescript.md

---
title: "TypeScript"
description: "Types ship in the npm package. CI checks them on TypeScript 7 and 6."
---

# TypeScript

The published packages include their `.d.ts` files. A value's type is inferred from the Zod schema you pass in.

```ts
import { z } from "zod";
import { transformSchema, type Config } from "@adaptate/core";

const recipe = z.object({ title: z.string(), servings: z.number() });
type Recipe = z.infer<typeof recipe>;
const card = { title: true } satisfies Config<Recipe>;
const cardSchema = transformSchema(recipe.partial(), card);
```

`scripts/ts-consumer-check.mjs` packs `@adaptate/core` and `@adaptate/utils`, installs the tarballs, and typechecks a consumer that imports every published entry.

The CI job `ts7-consumer` runs that script on TypeScript 7 and TypeScript 6, each with `moduleResolution` `bundler`, `node16`, and `nodenext`.

Dev TypeScript in this repo is 7.0.2. Lint is `oxlint --type-aware` (`oxlint-tsgolint`), including `typescript/no-deprecated`.


# Subpaths

Source: docs/subpaths.md

---
title: "Subpaths"
description: "The published entry points, and which peers each one loads."
---

# Subpaths

`@adaptate/core` publishes five entries and has no `dependencies`. `zod@^3.25.0 || ^4.0.0` is the required peer. `effect@^4.0.0` is an optional peer and is imported only by `@adaptate/core/effect`.

```mermaid
flowchart LR
  zod["zod peer"] --> core["@adaptate/core"]
  zod --> stream["@adaptate/core/stream"]
  zod --> incremental["@adaptate/core/stream-incremental"]
  zod --> standard["@adaptate/core/standard"]
  zod --> effect["@adaptate/core/effect"]
  effectPeer["effect optional peer"] -.-> effect
```

| Entry | Exports |
| --- | --- |
| `@adaptate/core` | `transformSchema`, `makeConditionalSchemaTransformer`, `transformPartialSchema`, `validatePartialAgainstConfigs`, `makeStreamingConditionalTransformer`, `Config`, `DeepPartial`, `PartialValidationResult` |
| `@adaptate/core/stream` | `parsePartialJson`, `createStreamValidator`, `validateStructuredOutput`, `createAgUiPartialValidator`, `agUiValidatorWith`, `reparseFeed`, `createFrameThrottle`, `AgUiDeltaEvent`, `PartialJsonFeed` |
| `@adaptate/core/stream-incremental` | `createPartialJsonFeed`, `fromAsyncIterable`, `createAgUiPartialValidator`, `PartialJsonFeed` |
| `@adaptate/core/standard` | `isStandardSchema`, `validateStandard`, `validateAgainstStandardSchemas`, `StandardSchemaV1`, `StandardIssue`, `StandardResult`, `StandardValidationResult` |
| `@adaptate/core/effect` | `validate`, `validatePartial`, `createEffectStreamValidator`, `AdaptateValidationError`, `AdaptateParseError`, `ConfigReport`, `FinalReport` |

`@adaptate/utils` has no required runtime dependencies. Its peers are in [Optional peers](optional-peers.md). Published paths:

| Import | Runtime file |
| --- | --- |
| `@adaptate/utils` | `build/index.es.js` (browser bundle; Node builtins are external) |
| `@adaptate/utils/openapi` | `ssr-build/openapi.js` |
| `@adaptate/utils/ssr` | `ssr-build/index.js` |

Use `/ssr` or `/openapi` when loading a spec from disk.


# Optional peers

Source: docs/optional-peers.md

---
title: "Optional peers"
description: "effect, js-yaml, and the ref parser load only when that code is imported."
---

# Optional peers

| Package | Peer | When it loads |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `@adaptate/core` | `effect@^4.0.0` | Only `@adaptate/core/effect` |
| `@adaptate/utils` | `js-yaml@^5.5.0` | Only while parsing YAML |
| `@adaptate/utils` | `@apidevtools/json-schema-ref-parser@^16.0.8` | Only for a remote or file `$ref` |

`zod@^3.25.0 || ^4.0.0` is required for both packages. Neither package has a `dependencies` field.

In-document `$ref` pointers use the local resolver (`packages/utils/src/dereference-local.ts`). JSON specs need no extra package.

A missing YAML parser throws:

```
Optional peer dependency "js-yaml" is required to parse YAML. Install it with `pnpm add js-yaml`.
```

A missing ref parser throws:

```
Optional peer dependency "@apidevtools/json-schema-ref-parser" is required to resolve remote or file $ref pointers. Install it with `pnpm add @apidevtools/json-schema-ref-parser`.
```

js-yaml 5 ships its own types. `@types/js-yaml` is not a dependency.


# Performance

Source: docs/performance.md

---
title: "Performance"
description: "Measured cost of import, a full document, four component views, a streaming check, and bundle size."
---

# Performance

CI compares a pull request with its base (`scripts/bench-compare.mjs`) and fails when any case is more than 5% slower (limit `1.05`). Cases: `transformSchema`, `transformPartialSchema`, `parsePartialJson`, `agUiStream`, `deepTransform`. `deepTransform` builds one 200-level object schema outside the timed loop and times `transformSchema` only.

Zod's own `safeParse` still walks a schema by recursion. The 100,000-level checks walk documents and partial JSON. They do not call it.

| Function | Walk | Reason |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `completeJson`, `parsePartialJson`, `reparseFeed` | loop | Partial JSON text can nest without bound |
| `createPartialJsonFeed` | loop | A stream chunk can deepen the same document |
| `openAPISchemaToZod`, `zodToOpenAPISchema` | loop | An OpenAPI document is runtime input |
| `dereferenceLocalDocument`, `deepMergeResolvedValue`, `documentContainsExternalRef` | loop | A local `$ref` document is runtime input |
| `transformSchema`, `extendSchema` | recursive | Schema depth is the source that declares it |
| `unwrapOptional`, `lenientSchema`, `partialSchemaFor` | recursive | Same bound. A deeper value overflows inside `safeParse` |
| `makeConditionalSchemaTransformer`, `schemasForConfigs` | one level | They do not walk nested fields |
| `isOptional` | one check | It does not walk children |

The [#53](https://github.com/p10ns11y/adaptate/pull/53) run reported:

| Case | Ratio (head / base) |
| --- | --- |
| `transformSchema` | 1.043 |
| `transformPartialSchema` | 1.002 |
| `parsePartialJson` | 0.989 |
| `agUiStream` | 0.996 |

[DESIGN.md](../DESIGN.md) estimates the traversal at O(N) time and O(D) space. That note is not a measured benchmark.

## Measured

Zod and valibot: no repair, needs complete JSON." src="../assets/perf.svg" width="960">

Node v24.22.3. Commit [`1a51df5`](https://github.com/p10ns11y/adaptate/commit/1a51df50ff0842213e015b18c5d4240a2e994c0a). One local `node bench/ab/run.js`. [Performance](#ab-versus-raw-zod)

`@adaptate/core/stream-incremental` tokenizes a partial JSON stream once. The grocery order is 966 characters, and `visits` is 966. A full rescan was 68,304 character visits. AG-UI on that subpath is 3.023 µs/chunk. Parsed partial is 0.835 µs/chunk against raw Zod 0.606 µs/chunk. [Incremental partial JSON](incremental-parser.md)

## A/B versus raw Zod

```mermaid
flowchart LR
  order[Grocery order JSON]
  deltas[TOOL_CALL_ARGS deltas]
  order --> A[A raw zod]
  order --> B[B zod plus adaptate]
  order --> C[C valibot]
  deltas --> A
  deltas --> B
  deltas --> C
  A --> node[Node 24]
  B --> node
  C --> node
  node --> gate[Gate head vs base, 5%]
  A --> recorded[Bun and Chromium]
  B --> recorded
  C --> recorded
```

One grocery order, three validators. [`agree.js`](../bench/ab/agree.js) checks they accept and reject the same fixtures, including every stream chunk, before a number is kept.

```sh
pnpm --filter @adaptate/core build && node bench/ab/run.js
```

| Row | What is timed |
| --- | --- |
| Full document | One `safeParse` of a schema built once. B is one `transformSchema` of the all-optional base plus `receiptConfig`. |
| Import | Module eval plus one full-document validation. Node and Bun: a fresh process per sample, one discarded warmup, then 31 samples. Chromium: a fresh page, no discarded warmup. The browser bundle includes this harness on every variant, so the B minus A import delta cancels it. Node and Bun import the package entry. |
| Bundle | esbuild, minify, tree-shaking. Full bundle, and a second bundle with `zod` external. `effect` is always external. |

Where the work is not the same:

- AG-UI: B imports `createAgUiPartialValidator` from `@adaptate/core/stream-incremental`. Each chunk is tokenized once ([incremental scan](incremental-parser.md)), then `safeParse`s a lenient schema cached on the base schema when the value is new. A and C do not repair partial JSON. They need a complete value, so the chart marks them `no repair: needs complete JSON`. `repairMicros` clocks `parsePartialJson` from `@adaptate/core/stream` on the growing buffer, without the check. That clock is the full-prefix oracle. It is recorded and is not gated.
- Parsed partial: the same value. B reuses one lenient schema per base schema (`WeakMap`) and `safeParse`s it. A and C reuse one static all-optional schema. The `ab-eval` gate names this row `adaptate cached partial us/chunk` and fails when head is more than 5% slower than base.
- `./standard` and `./effect` are bundle rows only. The timed app does not call the effect wrapper.
- Valibot uses its own schemas for the same accept/reject rules.
- `createStreamValidator.final()` is not the full-document row. The validator builds one `transformSchema` result per config when it is created and reuses it. A direct `transformSchema` call still builds a schema each time, which is what the full-document row does once, outside the timed loop.
- Four views per render: card, line items, delivery, and receipt. The schemas are built once. Each timed render parses the grocery order with all four. Zod and Valibot use static schemas for those fields. Adaptate calls `transformSchema` on one partial schema. The rate is renders per second (`viewsPerSec`). [`agree.js`](../bench/ab/agree.js) requires the full order to pass every view, and an empty object or a card-only object to fail. This row is recorded and is not gated. The README chart does not draw it.

The `ab-eval` job gates Node only, head build against the base commit, and fails above 5%: adaptate import median, full-document validations/sec, AG-UI µs/chunk (`@adaptate/core/stream-incremental`), cached parsed-partial µs/chunk, and min plus gzip bytes for `.`, `./stream`, `./stream-incremental`, `./standard`, and `./effect` (full bundle and zod-external). `./stream-incremental` is new on this line, so its base is the recorded size in `bench/ab/config.js` until a base commit contains that entry. Timings are interleaved and re-measured up to three times. Bundle bytes are not re-measured. Import p95, JSON repair, four views per render, heap after `node --expose-gc`, the raw-zod control rows, Bun, and Chromium are uploaded with the job summary and are not gated. A positive time in B vs A is slower. A negative validations/sec is slower.

On the same runner, the gate compared `233b1ef17f994088cc5687c0c5ea61ff7a7751a9` with the base commit (no schema cache). Parsed-partial went from 178.740 µs/chunk to 0.731 µs/chunk (ratio 0.004). AG-UI went from 206.137 µs/chunk to 20.571 µs/chunk (ratio 0.100). Full-document rate went from 3120065.726/s to 3263762.591/s (ratio 1.046). Import median went from 36.832 ms to 36.476 ms (ratio 0.990). The gate passed (limit 1.05).

The table below is one local `node bench/ab/run.js` of commit `1a51df50ff0842213e015b18c5d4240a2e994c0a` against raw Zod and Valibot. It is not the gate. The AG-UI row is `createAgUiPartialValidator` from `@adaptate/core/stream-incremental`. For A and C that full push is the parsed-partial check, because they have no repair step. `repairMicros` is `parsePartialJson` on the growing buffer and is not that row.

Node v24.22.3, Bun 1.4.5, and Chromium 159.0.8154.6.

Workload: grocery order, 966 bytes, 41 `TOOL_CALL_ARGS` deltas. `deltaCharacters` is 24, and the last delta is the remainder. Import time includes module evaluation and one full-document validation. Node and Bun use a fresh process per sample, median and p95 of 31 samples after one discarded warmup. Chromium uses a fresh page per sample and no discarded warmup. Full-document and per-chunk rates are the median of 11 passes of 200 ms, one variant per process (Node, Bun) or page (Chromium). Node and Bun clocks are `process.hrtime.bigint`. The browser clock is `performance.now`.

`@adaptate/core/stream-incremental` reads each character of that grocery order once. Partial JSON tests assert `visits` equals the text length. [`scripts/render-perf-chart.mjs`](../scripts/render-perf-chart.mjs) reads [`assets/perf-run.json`](../assets/perf-run.json) and fails if a field is missing.

## Credit

Measure first, then optimize only the critical path. Donald E. Knuth, "Structured Programming with go to Statements", ACM Computing Surveys 6(4), 1974:

> We should forget about small efficiencies, say about 97% of the time: premature optimization is the root of all evil. Yet we should not pass up our opportunities in that critical 3%.

The per-chunk re-parse was that critical 3% here: [10.1145/356635.356640](https://doi.org/10.1145/356635.356640). Section 2 (pp. 280-285) replaces nested calls with loops and an explicit stack, so a document nested without bound does not overflow the host call stack.


# Proof

Source: docs/proof.md

---
title: "Proof"
description: "Each front-page sentence mapped to a test, a script, or a CI job."
---

# Proof

Each sentence on the front page maps to something in the repo.

| Sentence | Proof |
| --- | --- |
| Partial documents fail a full schema, and deep input overflows a recursive walk | The rows below. `JSON.parse` throws on a cut-off tool call. The deep walks covered here keep their frames in an ordinary stack |
| 100,000 levels. Streamed JSON, including a missing last character | [`reads streamed JSON one hundred thousand levels deep`](../packages/core/src/__tests__/deep-nesting.test.ts) expects the leaf `1` from `createPartialJsonFeed`, `reparseFeed`, `parsePartialJson`, and `parsePartialJson` of the text with the last character removed |
| 100,000 levels. OpenAPI to Zod, Zod to OpenAPI, and a local `$ref` document | [`converts an OpenAPI schema one hundred thousand levels deep`](../packages/utils/src/__tests__/deep-nesting.test.ts), [`converts a Zod schema one hundred thousand levels deep`](../packages/utils/src/__tests__/deep-nesting.test.ts), and [`dereferences a document one hundred thousand levels deep`](../packages/utils/src/__tests__/deep-nesting.test.ts) |
| Under 3 seconds. One `$ref` at each of those 100,000 levels | [`resolves one ref at each of one hundred thousand levels`](../packages/utils/src/__tests__/deep-nesting.test.ts) expects `performance.now()` around `dereferenceLocalDocument` to be under `3_000` |
| `RangeError` past 500. A nested `$ref` chain stops at depth 500 | That same file builds a 2,000-link chain and expects `RangeError` matching `Maximum dereference depth (500)`. [`resolves a local pointer chain and rejects nested refs past 500`](../packages/utils/src/__tests__/dereference-local.test.ts) expects the same error for a chain of 501 |
| `JSON.parse` throws `SyntaxError`. `check.partial` is `{ title: "Pas" }`. `check.results.card.valid` is `true` | [`readme snippets`](../packages/core/src/__tests__/index.test.ts). The same partial shape is covered for a shorter cut in [`stream.test.ts`](../packages/core/src/__tests__/stream.test.ts) |
| The same partial reader returns the leaf of a 100,000-level document with the last character missing | The streamed-JSON case above, `parsePartialJson(text.slice(0, -1))` |
| Streams partial JSON without re-reading what it already saw | Partial JSON tests assert `visits` equals the text length ([`partial-json.property.test.ts`](../packages/core/src/__tests__/partial-json.property.test.ts), [`stream.test.ts`](../packages/core/src/__tests__/stream.test.ts)). The recorded run is [Measured](performance.md#measured) |
| `{ title: "Pas" }` passes that card. The same schema with `servings: true` rejects it | [`readme snippets`](../packages/core/src/__tests__/index.test.ts). [examples/react-view](../examples/react-view) renders the card and the kitchen |
| Three deltas give `{ title: "Pa" }`, `{ title: "Pasta" }`, `{ title: "Pasta", servings: 2 }`. `final({ title: "Pasta" })` passes the card and not the kitchen | [`readme snippets`](../packages/core/src/__tests__/index.test.ts) `streams three deltas and reports per-view readiness from final` |
| Nested fields, `"*"` array items, `satisfies Config<T>`, and `requiredIf` | [`readme snippets`](../packages/core/src/__tests__/index.test.ts) `checks nested, array, and conditional configs` |
| OpenAPI to Zod and back keeps `required` | [`readme snippets`](../packages/utils/src/__tests__/openapi.test.ts) `converts an OpenAPI schema to Zod and back` |
| `fromAsyncIterable` reads bytes from a Node `Readable` | [`readme snippets`](../packages/core/src/__tests__/index.test.ts) `reads bytes from a Node Readable incrementally` |
| A transformed Zod schema works through `@adaptate/core/standard` | [`readme snippets`](../packages/core/src/__tests__/index.test.ts) `validates transformed Zod schemas as Standard Schemas`, and [`standard.test.ts`](../packages/core/src/__tests__/standard.test.ts) |
| `createEffectStreamValidator(...).final(text)` reports each view | [`readme snippets`](../packages/core/src/__tests__/index.test.ts) `reports views from the Effect validator`, and [`effect.test.ts`](../packages/core/src/__tests__/effect.test.ts) |
| A circular schema passed to either converter throws `RangeError` | [`openapi.test.ts`](../packages/utils/src/__tests__/openapi.test.ts) `throws when a dereferenced schema points at an ancestor` and `throws when an object getter refers to its own schema` |
| Two performance gates fail a pull request more than 5% slower or larger than its base | [`bench` and `ab-eval`](../.github/workflows/ci.yml). Numbers in [Performance](performance.md) |
| Types ship in the package. CI checks the packed tarballs on TypeScript 7 and 6, for `bundler`, `node16`, and `nodenext` | [`@adaptate/core` publishes `types`](../packages/core/package.json). [`ts7-consumer`](../.github/workflows/ci.yml) runs [`ts-consumer-check.mjs`](../scripts/ts-consumer-check.mjs) |

`transformSchema` is checked at 1,000 levels in [`walks a schema one thousand levels deep`](../packages/core/src/__tests__/deep-nesting.test.ts). That walk is still recursive. A deeper value overflows inside Zod's own `safeParse`. The 100,000-level rows above do not call it.

Peers, subpaths, and the Effect method names are in [Optional peers](optional-peers.md), [Subpaths](subpaths.md), and [Effect](effect.md).


# Migration 2.4

Source: docs/migration-2.4.md

---
title: "Migration 2.4"
description: "YAML and the ref parser became optional peers between 2.3 and 2.4."
---

# Migration 2.3 → 2.4

Published 2.3.0 of `@adaptate/utils` depended on `@apidevtools/json-schema-ref-parser@^15.3.5` and `js-yaml@^4.1.1`.

2.4 makes both optional:

- Install `js-yaml@^5.5.0` if you parse YAML.
- Install `@apidevtools/json-schema-ref-parser@^16.0.8` if you resolve remote or file `$ref`s.
- In-document `$ref`s stay on the local resolver. JSON specs need neither package.

[#51](https://github.com/p10ns11y/adaptate/pull/51) moved those packages from parser 15 and js-yaml 4 to parser 16 and js-yaml 5, and dropped `@types/js-yaml` because js-yaml 5 ships its types. The Zod peer stays `^3.25.0 || ^4.0.0`. `@adaptate/core` still has no runtime dependencies.

`@adaptate/core/standard` validates a Standard Schema (`~standard.validate`) and adds no dependency. The test uses a transformed Zod schema and a hand-written schema ([`standard.test.ts`](../packages/core/src/__tests__/standard.test.ts)).

`@adaptate/core/effect` is new. Install `effect@^4.0.0` only if you import it. `final(text)` and `final(text, configName)` are in [Effect](effect.md).


# Development

Source: docs/development.md

---
title: "Development"
description: "Install, test, and build this repository with pnpm."
---

# Development

Install and build this repo with pnpm. Root `package.json` sets `"packageManager": "pnpm@11.1.1"`. `.npmrc` and `pnpm-workspace.yaml` set lifecycle restrictions, store integrity, and the release-age gate. `npm install` at the repo root is unsupported: npm does not apply those settings, and the tree can diverge from CI.

`pnpm add` / `npm install` of the published `@adaptate/*` packages is how consumers install from the registry.

`pnpm docs:api` rewrites [docs/api](api/index.md) from the built `.d.ts` files, and rewrites `llms.txt` and `llms-full.txt`. Run it after `pnpm build`. The verify job fails when those files drift.

Engines: the repo and `@adaptate/core` require Node `>=24`. `@adaptate/utils` declares Node `>=20`.

```sh
pnpm install
pnpm lint
pnpm test          # check-types, then vitest run --coverage
pnpm test:watch
pnpm build         # turbo run build
pnpm typecheck
```

`turbo.json` makes `build` depend on dependency `check-types` and dependency `test`.

```
├── .devcontainer/   # Node 24 + pnpm
├── bench/ab/        # A/B runtime eval
├── docs/
├── packages/core/   # @adaptate/core
├── packages/utils/  # @adaptate/utils
├── skills/
├── tools/api-docs/  # TypeDoc markdown from the published .d.ts files
├── AGENTS.md
├── CODING_STYLE.md
└── turbo.json
```

Agent procedures: [AGENTS.md](../AGENTS.md), [skills/](../skills/). Dev container: [.devcontainer/README.md](../.devcontainer/README.md).

The pattern comes from [Oneflow AB](https://oneflow.com): one data model, several components, different required fields. The first prototype was a ChatGPT Canvas. PR [#21](https://github.com/p10ns11y/adaptate/pull/21) is the first agent-written change in the repo.

License: MIT.

# Function: validate()

> **validate**\<`TSchema`, `TConfig`\>(`schema`, `config`, `value`): `Effect`\<`output`\<`TSchema`\>, [`AdaptateValidationError`](../classes/AdaptateValidationError.md)\>

### TConfig

`TConfig` *extends* `boolean` \| \{ `*?`: [`Config`](../../index/type-aliases/Config.md)\<`unknown`\>; \} \| \{ \} \| `object` & `object`

## Parameters

### schema

# Type Alias: Config\<T\>

Source: docs/api/core/index/type-aliases/Config.md

---
title: "Type Alias: Config\\<T\\>"
description: "Type-safe configuration for `transformSchema` and conditional transformers."
---

# Type Alias: Config\<T\>

> **Config**\<`T`\> = `boolean` \| `unknown` *extends* `T` ? `object` & `object` : `T` *extends* readonly infer U[] ? `object` : `T` *extends* `object` ? `{ [K in keyof T]?: Config<T[K]> }` : `never`

Type-safe configuration for `transformSchema` and conditional transformers.

## High-value use cases this type enables:
- Full autocomplete for every field path in your schema
- Compile-time errors for typos or non-existent fields
- Natural support for deeply nested objects
- Special `'*'` syntax for array element configuration
- `true` = make required, `false` = keep optional (or omit)

## Type Parameters

### T

`T` = `unknown`

## Example

```ts
const config = {
  name: true,
  address: { city: true, country: false },
  tags: { '*': true },
} satisfies Config<z.infer<typeof mySchema>>;
```

# Function: openAPISchemaToZod()

Source: docs/api/utils/openapi/functions/openAPISchemaToZod.md

---

# Function: openAPISchemaToZod()

> **openAPISchemaToZod**(`schema`, `propertyKey?`, `required?`): `ZodType`

Converts an OpenAPI / JSON Schema object to a Zod schema.
Supports a wide range of features for feature-completeness:
- Primitives: string, number, integer, boolean
- Complex: object, array, enum
- Validations: min/max length, min/max, pattern, format (email, uuid, url, datetime, etc.)
- Combinators: allOf (intersection), anyOf/oneOf (union)
- Nullable
- Proper required field handling

Note: $ref should be pre-resolved by getDereferencedOpenAPIDocument.

## Parameters

### schema

`any`

### propertyKey?

`string`

### required?

`string`[]

## Returns

`ZodType`


# Function: zodToOpenAPISchema()

Source: docs/api/utils/openapi/functions/zodToOpenAPISchema.md

---
title: "Function: zodToOpenAPISchema()"
description: "Converts a Zod schema to an OpenAPI / JSON Schema compatible object. Now feature-complete with: - Proper `required` array for objects (excludes .optional() fields) - Support for..."
---

# Function: zodToOpenAPISchema()

> **zodToOpenAPISchema**(`zodSchema`): `any`

Converts a Zod schema to an OpenAPI / JSON Schema compatible object.
Now feature-complete with:
- Proper `required` array for objects (excludes .optional() fields)
- Support for .nullable()
- String validations: minLength, maxLength, pattern, format
- Number validations: minimum, maximum, exclusive*, multipleOf, integer
- Array minItems / maxItems
- Enum support
- Union / anyOf
- Description from .describe()
- Zod 4 attached checks (`_zod.def.checks`) and legacy `_def.checks` where present

## Parameters

### zodSchema

`ZodType`

## Returns

`any`
